title: Credit-smoothing admission controller for tiered service routing and elastic demotion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an admission controller that smooths per-tenant credits and enforces tier-aware routing decisions. This ticket designs and implements 'credit smoothing' (moving-average token buckets + decay) to avoid immediate hard-demotions for short burst usage while preserving priority for paid and enterprise tiers. The controller will sit at the regional gateway level, consult tenant credit states and tier policies, and return routing decisions: serve on preferred tier, redirect to lower-cost variant, or enqueue into a rescue queue for soft-fallback. Goals: protect SLAs for paying customers, reduce oscillation during traffic spikes, maintain predictable unit economics, and provide clear telemetry for policy effects.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller exposes an API that returns routing decision (serve/preempt/demote/enqueue) within 2ms p50 on regional gateways
Per-tenant credit smoothing implemented (EWMA window configurable) and persists to the credits store; smoothing window default 30s
System performs soft-demotion instead of instant hard blocks for short bursts: >=90% of 30s bursts are served with demotion instead of cancelation
Paid and enterprise tiers maintain 95th percentile latency SLO under 70% of baseline during combined burst traffic while free tier requests experience graceful capacity reduction
End-to-end integration tests cover scenarios: global burst, region failover, quota exhaustion, and cross-tenant fairness
Dashboard shows credit balance, smoothed consumption rates, demotion counts, and customer impact labels for last 30 days
tasks: Draft design doc: credit model, smoothing algorithm, and persistence layout
Prototype admission controller library (Go) with in-memory token smoothing
Integrate with credits store (Redis)/caching layer and design fallback persistence
Add tier policy configuration (free/paid/enterprise) and mapping to model variants
Implement rescue queue and soft-demotion logic with exponential backoff slots
End-to-end test harness and chaos tests for region spillover
Instrument telemetry and Grafana dashboard panels
Performance benchmarking and kernel-level latency profiling
Ship canary: region eu-west-1 -> 5% traffic -> monitor 72h -> ramp
tech_decisions: Use EWMA smoothing over fixed token bucket to blend short bursts and steady usage
Persist tenant credit deltas to Redis with per-region prefix; allow eventual consistency for non-critical decisions
Admission controller runs in the regional gateway process for lowest latency and direct access to routing
Soft-demotion preferred over hard-deny; demotion maps to cheaper quantized model variants or lower concurrency pool
Rescue queue is rate-limited and prioritized by tier and tenant historical SLA credit
Configurable policy flags: smoothing_window_s, demotion_threshold_pct, rescue_queue_size
rollouts: Deploy library to staging and run traffic replay against production traces
Canary in one low-traffic region (eu-west-1) at 5% for 72h
If p95 latency regressions >5% for paid tier, rollback and analyze
